articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Classification of Faults in Cable via Compressed Sensing Time-Domain Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In this paper, a new method for cable diagnostics is proposed based on compressed acquisition of Orthogonal Multi-tone Time Domain Reflectometry (OMTDR). In this study, the Random Demodulator (RD) is used to sample the reflected signals, and we propose a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) for classifying hard and soft faults in cables from compressed reflected signals without reconstruction. In our study, the training and test sets are obtained using a wireline diagnostic simulator. The classification results of the machine learning models demonstrate the high efficiency and accuracy of performing fault detection directly from the compressed data, with all fault types classified with an accuracy of over 99%.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Attention Convolution Subdomain Adaption Network for Cross-Domain Fault Diagnosis of Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Transfer learning method represented by domain adaptation has achieved great success in cross-domain fault diagnosis of machine. However, there are still some issues to be addressed to further improve diagnostic performance. First, most existing methods extract features from a single scale, which may lose useful multi-scale feature information from vibration signals. Second, most of the existing methods majorly align the source and target distributions from a global perspective to reduce distribution discrepancy across domains, which ignores the relationship of the corresponding subdomains from the same category in different domains and leads to unsatisfying transfer learning results. To solve these issues, a multi-scale attention convolution subdomain adaption network is proposed for mechanical fault diagnosis under cross-domain conditions. Firstly, a multi-scale attention convolution block is built to extract and adaptively fuse multi-scale fault features. Secondly, the local maximum mean discrepancy metric is introduced to align the subdomain distributions of the source and target domains. The proposed method is evaluated based on six different transfer diagnostic tasks under variable speeds in case study, and the experimental results verify its adaptability and advantage over other advanced methods.

articleTitle: Overview of Vehicle Chassis Fault Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The information and networking of armored vehicles are the important development directions of Chinese Army weapon equipment. Fault detection Armed vehicle chassis is an advanced vehicle system designed to improve the reliability and safety of armed vehicles. By monitoring the parameters of the vehicle chassis in real time, such as vibration, temperature, pressure and wear, the system can quickly detect potential faults or problems, and take appropriate measures to prevent or solve the faults in time. Fault detection Armed vehicle chassis adopts high-precision sensor and advanced algorithm to monitor and analyze the working state of vehicle chassis in real time. It can not only reduce the failure rate of armed vehicles, reduce maintenance costs, but also improve the combat effectiveness and survivability of vehicles. In the future war, fault detection of armed vehicle chassis will become one of the key technologies to improve the mobility and combat effectiveness of troops. This paper will summarize the research of vehicle chassis in recent years.

articleTitle: Fault Impact Extraction for Planetary Gearbox Using Motor Current
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: As the widely used transmission components, planetary gearboxes are prone to failure because of working under heavy loads. Hence, fault diagnosis is a key to guaranteeing the reliability of planetary gearboxes. In this field, motor current signal analysis (MCSA) is a new rising technology. Traditional MCSA just focuses on spectrum identification. However, the local spectrum is masked by other components in the global spectrum and is hard to identify. Therefore, it is necessary to research novel methods to extract fault impact from motor current. In this article, a new variational mode decomposition based adaptive comb filtering method is introduced to extract fault impacts from motor current. Then, experiments are carried out to validate the performance. The results show that the variational mode decomposition based adaptive comb filtering can extract fault impact from motor current efficaciously.

articleTitle: Compound Fault Diagnosis of Planetary Gearbox Using Capsule Network with Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Capsule network is an innovative deep learning-based model that uses neuron vectors as inputs and outputs of the network. It can achieve independent output of multiple classification labels, and solve the problem of decoupling recognition of compound fault components in planetary gearboxes. However, the single-scale feature extraction cannot fully explore multi-scale feature information in compound fault signals. This study proposes a capsule network combined with multi-scale convolutional feature fusion to diagnose the compound fault of planetary gearbox. The multi-scale features are extracted from STFT images of vibration signals using convolutional layers with different kernel sizes; secondly, a capsule network is designed to classify and identify the fault components by using the dynamic routing algorithm. The experiments are conducted to assess the performance of the proposed method, and the results indicates that it can effectively decoupling identify the compound faults with strong anti-interference and stability.

articleTitle: Enhanced Data Augmentation for Bearing Fault Diagnosis by Using a Spectral Flow Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: While existing flow-based models have the potential for data enhancement and intelligent fault diagnosis of bearings, these methods are mainly based on the time domain to learn features. In general, time-domain and frequency-domain features are important for recognizing faults. Especially, the spectral features in the frequency domain can reveal highly distinct patterns associated with fault types. Therefore, learning spectral feature helps to obtain comprehensive fault information and achieve high fault diagnosis accuracy. In this work, a spectral flow model framework is developed to learn and generate realistic data from mechanical sensor signals. The performance of fault diagnosis under unbalanced data is improved by learning the information contained in the spectral features, which are utilized to generate insufficient fault data. Experimental results show that the present method can generate a large number of samples with higher similarity and better diversity on the bearing dataset. The generated samples may be used to expand the limited dataset and significantly improve the accuracy of the bearing fault diagnosis task.

articleTitle: Design of a Marine Litter Collection Apparatus Utilizing Wave and Wind Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Marine litter, characterized by its abundant presence, widespread distribution, and consequential environmental hazards, poses significant challenges for effective management. Conventional collection methodologies are afflicted by inefficiencies, exorbitant costs, and inadequate responsiveness. In response to these challenges, this paper introduces a novel apparatus designed for marine litter collection. Harnessing the kinetic potential of wave and wind energy, this apparatus features a dynamically adjustable V-shaped interception net, complemented by a robust litter retrieval system and supplementary auxiliary components. Through the utilization of wave and wind-driven interception structures, litter is effectively captured and directed towards designated storage units for periodic removal. The conceptualization and realization of this apparatus serve to mitigate the prevailing shortcomings associated with marine litter collection, notably addressing issues of temporal efficacy and resource consumption. Consequently, it presents a promising avenue towards the attainment of sustainable, efficient, and automated management strategies for marine litter.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Estimation Based on the System Trajectory in a Latent Space Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Latent variable models such as Variational Autoen-coders (VAE) are widely used to analyze complex systems. These models allow for projecting time-oriented datasets defined in high-dimensional physical spaces into trajectories in the latent space, as evidenced in multiple case studies from the Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) literature. The present study introduces a general approach for estimating the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) from a kinematic description of a trajectory in the latent space. The approach is demonstrated on two synthetic trajectories, evidencing its pertinence for prognosis modeling from the latent space.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Maximum System Efficiency Under Power Allocation Conditions for One-to-Two MC-WPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In multi-load magnetically coupled wireless power transfer system (MC-WPT), the power distribution among multiple loads is also the research focus in multi-load WPT system. In this paper, we propose a system efficiency improvement control strategy under the power allocation condition of a two-load MC-WPT system with a conventional LCC-S type MC-WPT system. And in the paper, the power characteristics of the LCC-S system are analyzed, and a control strategy is proposed to compute the optimal fundamental voltage at the primary side, and this scheme adjusts the phase shift angle of the primary inverter to make the output fundamental voltage of the primary inverter reach the calculated optimal value, and at the same time adjusts the duty cycle of the secondary DC-DC module to make the output power of the system a set value. In this case, the efficiency of the system is maximized, the control method is simple and there is no need for primary and secondary side communication.

articleTitle: A Review of PHM Research on Weapons and Mechanical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: With the continuous improvement of complexity, accuracy, automation, and intelligence in weapon mechanical systems, PHM technology has emerged, effectively ensuring the safe and reliable operation and economic maintenance of mechanical equipment., When facing weapon systems with complex composition, multiple levels of product agreements, and a large number of modules, many scholars choose to study the subsystems of equipment to complete tasks such as status monitoring, fault detection, and fault isolation. In the research of subsystems, deep learning theory has received widespread attention from academia and industry, providing new ideas and technical means for solving fault prediction and health management problems in the context of big data. Therefore, the author summarizes the research results of deep learning in various subsystems of weapon machinery and equipment.

articleTitle: 3D Reconstruction of Aircraft Engine Damaged Blades Based on Monocular Vision
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: To improve the accuracy and speed of engine blade damage monitoring, this study considers using a monocular imaging device for 3D reconstruction of the damaged blades. Firstly, the SIFT is employed to extract and match feature points from the image sequence. Then, the SFM is utilized to generate a sparse point cloud structure. Finally, the dense point cloud structure is generated using the PMVS, and a 3D reconstruction model of the damaged blades is constructed. By comparing the damage size of reconstructed leaves with actual leaves, an error of approximately 0.004% is found, indicating that the 3D reconstruction model in this study is ideal.

articleTitle: Prediction of Crankshaft Bearing Wear Degree Based on ICEEMDAN-ZOA-GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Diesel engine is an important power equipment for a variety of vehicles. Its quality affects personal safety and normal running of vehicles. Using modern information technology to diagnose faults can improve diagnostic accuracy and efficiency. Taking a certain type of armored vehicle diesel engine as the research object, By using Intrinsic Computing Expressive Empirical Mode Decomposition With Adaptive Noise and combining with singular value decomposition to extract the signal features, Zebra optimization algorithm is used to optimize the gated cycle unit neural network for training prediction. The experimental results show that the prediction result of ZOA-GRU is up to 98%, which is 6% higher than that of the unoptimized gated cycle unit, and provides a basis for fault diagnosis of diesel engines.

Author Keywords: Intrinsic Computing Expressive Empirical Mode Decomposition With Adaptive Noise

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Partial Wear of TBM Disc Cutter
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In tunnel construction with Tunnel boring machines (TBMs), accurate knowledge of disc cutter failure states is crucial for ensuring efficient operation and preventing delays and cost overruns. This study investigates the influence of partial wear on disc cutter excavation parameters in shield tunneling operations. Meticulously designed experimental setups and procedures were employed to obtain precise excavation parameters, enabling faithful replication of the excavation process. The experimental apparatus, including a scaled-down shield test rig, adhered closely to similarity criteria with an actual shield. Careful designs of the cutterhead and disc cutters allowed for the simulation of various wear scenarios. Comprehensive data collection facilitated real-time analysis of excavation parameters, enhancing the scholarly robustness of the study. The investigation focused on the impact of failure states of disc cutters on torque and thrust, critical metrics for assessing shield tunneling efficiency. Results indicated that increasing partial-wear rates of disc cutters led to distinctive trends in mean and standard deviation of torque and thrust, revealing the complex interplay between partial wear and excavation parameters.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-driven Condition Monitoring: Development for Ball Screw Feed Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel digital twin (DT) framework designed for condition monitoring. In general, the current condition monitoring solutions suffer from challenges such as the availability of historical data, transferability, interoperability, scalability, etc. The framework shows the importance of DT in handling the first two challenges. The framework has four layers, i.e., physical, virtual, interaction, and decision. The framework performance has been shown for preload loss monitoring in ball screw feed drive systems. However, the framework is very generic and can be easily adapted to other rotating machinery applications such as bearings, gears, etc. The framework enables the extraction of key parameters such as natural frequency and logarithmic decrement from the time domain dynamic signal of the physical asset, which is used for updating the virtual model's parameters, representing the real-time interaction between the physical asset and the virtual counterpart. The interaction layer is capable of updating the parameters of its virtual counterpart to minimize discrepancies between actual and virtual responses. The decision layer in the framework is introduced to facilitate real-time predictive maintenance action or feedback error compensation using the potential of artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Vibration Reduction of a Tile Structure Using Tuned Mass Damper
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) technique can be applied as a mechanical concept for vibration reduction. In Structure Health Management (SHM), it is important to save the structure from possible damage and maintain unwanted vibrations as low as possible. When a structure or mechanical system experiences high vibration at the resonance frequency, this technique is efficient in suppressing the amplitude at this frequency. In the current article, TMD is applied to a tile structure that is designed for power generation. The structure experiences resonance high vibration due to an external vibration source. The natural frequency is evaluated for the tile structure as a 1DOF and then after adding the TMD system as a 2DOF. The results show effective vibration amplitude suppression. The added TMD is a small applicable system that saves the structure health from the damage that might happen due to the high resonance vibration and it can be easily disassembled when the risk of the external excitation source is removed.

articleTitle: Variational Residual Model for Machinery Condition Monitoring Under Complex Degradation Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Deep-learning based approaches have been widely used for constructing health indicator from machinery monitoring signals. However, the constructed health indicators (HIs) perform unstable under complex degradation processes. To address the problem, a variational residual network (VRN) is proposed in this paper. By implanting variational mechanism in the forward propagation network, VRN could infer the distribution characteristics of the monitor signals during degradation processes. Compared with the existing methods under turbopump bearing degradation dataset, health indicators constructed by the VRN perform higher monotonicity and trendability.

articleTitle: Research on SDN Load Balancing and Failure Handling Based on Dynamic Decision
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In the software defined network with multiple controllers, a logically centralized and physically distributed cluster of controllers is used to manage the switches throughout the network, achieving good scalability and management flexibility. However, the performance and security of the control plane are threatened by unbalanced network traffic requests, external attacks, and network failures. Therefore, for the problem of distributed controller load balancing and failures in software defined network, this paper proposes a dynamic decision load balancing and failure handling mechanism for SDN. Firstly, each controller will synchronise the load information and switch information of its domain to the distributed database. Then the decision controller is selected to determine the migration operation of the switch under overload or failure controller using the proposed multi-constrained load balancing algorithm and failure handling mechanism. Simulation results show that the research in this paper can effectively improve the load balancing of each controller, and it can also improve the throughput performance of the controller plane.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of AUV Propeller Based on Interference Suppression CLSTM-CNN-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) are indispensable equipment in underwater detection, surveying, and investigation, and thruster fault diagnosis is crucial to ensure the safe navigation of AUVs. However, due to the uncertainty of the underwater environment and the unpredictable occurrence of faults, this task is full of challenges. Therefore, we propose a CLSTM-CNN-Attention method for interference suppression for AUV thruster fault diagnosis. Specifically, we introduce a new network structure that combines the improved Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) in a parallel connection to simultaneously capture the temporal and spatial fault information of the input signal. At the same time, we also introduced a new linear rectification function to improve the model's anti-interference ability. Finally, by adding attention mechanisms to further improve diagnostic performance, the fused information can be better focused on. Experimental results have shown that our proposed method has strong interference suppression ability and outperforms other methods, demonstrating good performance in AUV fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Surrogate Model-Based Method for Multipurpose Overload Robot's Healthy Status Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Due to the extreme environment and large loads, the key components of the multipurpose overload robot sustained greater damage while performing maintenance tasks of the vacuum in the China Fusion Engineering Test Reactor (CFETR). It is necessary to monitor and predict the health status of these key compositions, avoiding safety incidents and economic losses. However, the lack of historical data poses a challenge in building performance evaluation models, while this simulation also requires a lot of computing power and time due to the system's complexity. A real-time high-fidelity monitoring and prediction methods are urgently required to meet the requirements of safe maintenance. Therefore, an effective surrogate model-based structure health status prediction method is proposed. At first, the Kriging model is built to represent the relationship between loads and stress of the CFETR multipurpose overload robot (CMOR)'s joint. Then, the rainflow counting method and S-N curve are leveraged to evaluate the cumulative damage according to the above stress spectrum. Finally, the joint 4# of CMOR is taken as an example to demonstrate the method, the model performs well and a key point's cumulative damage is calculated.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Acoustic Emission Guided Wave Technology in Radioactive Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Acoustic emission serves as an effective means for monitoring equipment status in radioactive environments. To address the unique challenges posed by such environments, waveguide rods are commonly employed to facilitate guided wave processing of acoustic emission signals at measurement points. The structural configuration of these waveguide rods significantly influences the attenuation of acoustic emission signals. Therefore, it is crucial to investigate the propagation attenuation behavior of acoustic emission signals in waveguide rods of varying sizes, as this knowledge holds great significance for the design and selection of appropriate waveguide rods. This paper employs a numerical simulation method to establish a computational model for analyzing the wave-guiding characteristics of waveguide rods. Experimental methods are used to explore the wave-guiding characteristics of waveguide rods of different sizes, and to validate the reliability of the simulation results. The findings demonstrate that the numerical simulation method provides a superior assessment of the wave-guiding characteristics. Moreover, it is observed that they are affected by specific dimensions of waveguide rods, with longer length and larger cross-sectional size rods exhibiting more evident attenuation of acoustic emission signals.

articleTitle: Control Strategy for Constant Voltage Regulation of Dual Active Bridge in MC-WPT System with LCC-LCC Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Electric vehicles are regarded as an effective solution to address the challenges of environmental pollution and energy shortage, and the endurance capacity of their batteries is undoubtedly the core issue restricting their development. The charging method has become the focus of research in academic circles at home and abroad. As a non-contact charging method, magnetic coupling wireless power transfer (MC-WPT) technology has become the main transmission mode of wireless charging systems for electric vehicles due to its significant advantages such as flexibility, safety, and high reliability. The national standard for wireless charging of electric vehicles recommends using a LCC-LCC resonant topology with constant current output as the standard topology of the system. Many scholars have conducted research on the steady-state constant voltage output control of the constant current topology. However, no one has yet proposed a constant voltage control method for the case of no load on the secondary side. This paper studies the constant voltage control strategy of the dual active bridge constant current output topology under no-load conditions.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Tunnel Illumination on Drivers' Physiological Indexes
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In order to explore the impact of tunnel illumination on drivers' physiological indicators, the changes of drivers' physiological indicators under different illumination levels and the reduction of illumination under safe driving conditions were determined. In this paper, the tunnel illumination data was collected by the illuminometer, the EEG index data of the driver was collected by the eego <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TM}$</tex> mylab EEG instrument, and the EEG data was processed by ASA software. The processed data was analyzed by SPSS, and it was found that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> wave had the most significant physiological response to the driver. The variation of illumination at the tunnel entrance and exit is much higher than that inside the tunnel. When the driver passes through the tunnel entrance and exit, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> wave presents a “jump” type change, from a stable state to a sudden increase trend, and then a stable regional fluctuation. When the illumination is less than 16001ux, the beta wave power is stable, and the illumination has little impact on the driver. When the illumination is higher than 20001ux, the EEG <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-wave power change at the tunnel entrance is significantly higher than that at the tunnel exit. It can be deduced that the illumination at the entrance of the tunnel has the greatest impact on the physiological load of the driver, followed by the exit of the tunnel, while the illumination at the middle of the tunnel has the least impact on the physiological load of the driver.

articleTitle: Design of the Fault Diagnosis and Maintenance Decision Support System for the Scientific Experiment Cabinets of Space Station
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In response to the large scale, diverse operating conditions, extensive data sources, and complex fault coupling characteristics of space station scientific experiment racks, a specialized system for space station scientific experiment cabinets fault diagnosis and maintenance decision support has been designed. This system is based on the Interface Data Sheets (IDS) and fault criterion logic, achieving graphical monitoring of parameter statuses by receiving engineering parameters, telemetry data, and other information from the payloads of the experimental cabinets. It autonomously diagnoses faults and isolates them to the orbital replacement units with precision and speed. The system effectively guides users in making maintenance decisions regarding the faulty orbital replacement units. Simultaneously, it can generate detailed maintenance information reports, offering decision support for on-orbit maintenance activities by astronauts. This paper provides a detailed introduction to the system's overall design concept and an overview of software function design. It offers a thorough and systematic description of each functional module. The development of this system not only furnishes the scientific experiment cabinets with comprehensive monitoring and fault diagnosis capabilities but also delivers efficient and accurate support for maintenance decision-making. This represents a pivotal technical assurance for the dependable operation of the space station's scientific experiment cabinets.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of Commonly Used Node.js Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: This paper first introduces what Node.js is. Then it analyzes several commonly used Node.js frameworks at present, such as Express, Koa, Hapi.js, Meteor, Nest.js and Egg.js. With some simple code and instructions of application of comparative, the advantages and disadvantages of each framework are analyzed. In the actual project, the framework can be selected according to the specific situation of the project.

articleTitle: From Fragments to Futures: Construction of Synthetic Run-to-Failure Trajectories for Fault State Prognostics
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Data-driven approaches for machine health state forecasting is dependent on the availability of run-to-failure (RTF) data in the condition monitoring history of the machines. In real industrial systems, maintenance interventions modify the natural degradation state evolution, keeping the machines in operable conditions. Moreover, inspections are conducted irregularly and with varying frequency, producing highly sparse data. Thus, degradation trajectory data are often not readily available in industrial machine inspection history. This lack of RTF data is a significant obstacle in the application of data-driven prognostics methods in the real world. This study proposes a graph based method to augment the partial trajectories from multiple machines to stitch together RTF data for complex machines. The study aims to show that diagnostics history showing machines in a range of possible health states is sufficient to generate prognostics information through these states. The proposed method is tested on a hydrogenerator prognostics case study with multiple fault states.

articleTitle: Cable Online Fault Diagnosis Technology Based on ZCZ Spread Spectrum Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: With the current increase in the number of aviation cables and the complexity of wiring, cable safety issues are becoming increasingly prominent. This paper addresses the problems of low diagnostic accuracy and high false alarm rates under high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) environments that existing cable detection methods struggle with. It analyzes the impact of noise interference on traditional Spread Spectrum Time Domain Reflectometry (SSTDR), summarizes the required characteristics of signals used for cable diagnostics in high SNR environments, and utilizes the Zero Correlation Zone (ZCZ) sequence's feature of having a low correlation coefficient with noise signals within its zero zone. A spread spectrum cable online fault diagnosis method based on the ZCZ sequence is proposed to improve diagnostic accuracy in high SNR environments. This paper verifies the superiority of the ZCZ sequence in cable fault diagnosis through simulations and experiments. The experimental results show that with an SNR not less than -10dB, the method achieves a fault detection accuracy higher than 95% and a false alarm rate lower than 2%.

articleTitle: Diagnostics and Prognostics for Retrofitted Systems: A Comprehensive Approach for Enhanced System Health Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life of technical systems has gained significant attention in recent years due to increasing demands for extending the lifespan of degrading system components. Therefore, already used systems are retrofitted by integrating sensors to monitor their performance and functionality, enabling accurate diagnosis of their condition and prediction of their remaining useful life. One of the main challenges in this field is identified in the missing data from the time where the retrofitted system has already run but without being monitored by sensors. In this paper, a novel approach for the combined diagnostics and prognostics of retrofitted systems is proposed. The methodology aims to provide an accurate diagnosis of the system's health state and estimation of the remaining useful life by a combination of a machine learning and expert knowledge. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology, a case study involving a retrofitted system in an industrial setting is selected and applied. It is demonstrated that the approach effectively diagnose the current system's health state and accurately predict its remaining useful life, thereby enabling predictive maintenance and decision-making. Overall, our research contributes to advancing the field of condition monitoring for retrofitted systems by providing a comprehensive methodology that addresses the challenge of missing data.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Overhead Transmission Line Ampacity Limit Driven by Non-Contact Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Rapidly growth of new energy generation capacity and electricity demand has brought new challenges on the existing power system. Dynamic rating technology is an effective way to improve power transmission capacity. The fixed combination of meteorological and operation state parameters is used to calculate the constant maximum thermal load capacity of overhead transmission lines in the traditional static thermal setting of power system, and the calculation results are often conservative. The sensing data-driven statistical analysis method are introduced in this paper to achieve dynamic setting of overhead transmission line current ampacity. Firstly, key parameters are determined based on standard line thermal equilibrium equation. Then, a data-driven carrying capacity model verification method is proposed to overcome the impact of perceived data quality and accuracy of carrying capacity models on the reliability of dynamic rating technology. On this basis, a dynamic evaluation method that combined with non-contact wire temperature and sag measurement for the transmission line ampacity limit is proposed. Finally, the feasibility of dynamic analysis of non-contact sensing and data-driven transmission line ampacity limit was verified through actual application cases. Results show that reasonable state perception parameter confidence levels and corresponding thermal rating can be easily determined based on the allowed operating risks of power grid.

articleTitle: Summary of Fault Prediction Algorithms for Fire Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Against the backdrop of the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology in the current computer field, various artificial intelligence related algorithms are widely used in the health management of weapon fire control systems. Fault detection is an important technology in weapon fire control system health management. By combining artificial intelligence algorithms with fault detection technology, the extracted fault feature information can more effectively improve the fault recognition and detection ability of weapon fire control systems. Therefore, The research on fault detection algorithms based on artificial intelligence is becoming a kind of the mainstream research directions, and this article will provide an overview of some related algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on Implementation Approaches for Delay Queue
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: This paper aims to explore and compare different implementation approaches for delay queue, which enjoy widespread applications in various scenarios that require the processing of delayed tasks, such as timed task scheduling and order timeout handling. As a special data structure, delay queue is widely used in various scenarios that require the processing of delayed tasks. This paper takes the order payment functionality of e-commerce platforms as a case study, exploring various implementation strategies for delay queues, including Delay Queue, Quartz, and Redis Sorted Set. Through comparative experiments, the paper analyzes the performance, reliability, and scalability of these methods and proposes corresponding improvement suggestions based on practical application scenarios. The research findings indicate that the selection of delay queue implementation methods should be comprehensively considered based on specific requirements, system architecture, and performance requirements. This study provides valuable references and insights for the implementation and application of delay queue.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Lifetime Prediction Method for Thermally Aged SiC MOSFET Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Power semiconductor switches, such as Metal-Oxide Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (MOSFETs), are widely utilized in solid-state power controllers (SSPC) of electric vehicles, aircrafts and trains. Predictive Health Monitoring (PHM), coupled with the reliability analysis of MOSFETs, are of ut-most significance in power electronic systems. Among various PHM indicators, the ON-state resistance of MOSFETs stands out as a vital and indicative harbinger of failure. This paper introduces a data-driven methodology employing a Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm to predict the variations of the ON-state resistance. The experimental dataset was derived from subjecting the MOSFET to power cycling under thermal stress conditions. Furthermore, the model's efficacy was scrutinized utilizing a minor fraction of the dataset for training the LSTM algorithm, showcasing robust performance. Additionally, the proposed model was validated across diverse MOSFET degradation datasets, affirming its universal applicability.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis and Comparison of Pre-Trained CNN in Bearing Fault Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: As deep learning methodologies progress, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are seeing growing application in image recognition, especially within the domain of bearing fault diagnosis. Utilizing CNN for the automatic identification of features in vibration-related images can enhance both accuracy and efficiency in bearing fault recognition. However, the industry has developed a number of pre trained CNN models and makes it demanding to select models for specific tasks of bearing fault diagnosis. Therefore, this paper aims to compare three of the main-trend CNN models' prediction accuracy and computational performance comprehensively. First, three pretrained CNN models-VGG16, ResNet and SqueezeNet, were trained to classify the bearing vibration signal dataset which had been converted to 2-D scalogram images. Transfer learning was applied to all models in this process. Then, the prediction accuracy and training time were examined and compared. Results showed that the accuracy of all CNN models were acceptable but SqueezeNet has the lowest runtime and highest accuracy. ResNet showed slightly lower performance and VGG16 experienced overfitting and produced the lowest accuracy with the longest runtime. Overall, for similar tasks of image-classification-based bearing fault diagnostics, SqueezeNet is a better candidate compared to other main stream pretrained CNN models, which can bring great accuracy accompanied with better efficiency. The findings of this work are good reference for future model selection in bearing fault diagnosis and related tasks.

articleTitle: Prediction for Remaining Useful Life of Lithium-ion Batteries Based on NGO-VMD and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of lithium-ion batteries is important in minimizing risks and ensuring safety. The capacity degradation signals exhibited by batteries possess non-stationarity and nonlinearity. To enhance the accuracy and stability of prediction results, the RUL prediction method based on the variational mode decomposition (VMD) optimized by Northern Goshawk Algorithm (NGO), combined with long short-term memory (LSTM) is proposed. First, we optimize two parameters of VMD using NGO. Subsequently, the optimized VMD was employed to decompose the capacity signal, and each IMF is then trained and predicted using LSTM. The final prediction was the summation of each component predictions. Three models were selected to verify the effectiveness of NGO-VMD-LSTM method in enhancing the RUL prediction accuracy of lithium-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Analysis of Vibration Fault Diagnosis Methods for Aeroengine
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Vibration is an important monitoring parameter for aircraft engines, and various vibration issues need to be addressed during engine testing. The reason why engine vibration is particularly important is that it directly affects the normal operation and lifespan of the engine. If the engine experiences abnormal vibration and is not checked and eliminated in a timely manner, it may cause serious consequences. Therefore, the diagnosis of vibration faults in aircraft engines has always been an important research topic in aircraft engine testing.

articleTitle: Research on Electrical Activity and Synchronization Behavior of Electromagnetic Coupled FHN Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: This paper proposes three models based on FHN neurons: a neuron model introducing a magnetic field variable through a magnetoresistive memristor, a neuron model introducing an external electric field, and a chain neural network model under the combined action of an electromagnetic field. (1) Detailed numerical simulations were performed on the two neuron models. The results show that under the action of a magnetic field, different external DC current stimulations and different feedback gains can lead to various discharge modes of neurons, such as resting state, spike discharge, and periodic spike discharge; while under the action of an electric field, different external DC current stimulations and different charge sizes can cause neurons to exhibit cluster discharges of different periods. (2) An in-depth analysis of the electromagnetic coupled neural network was conducted. The results found that increasing the synaptic coupling strength can enhance the synchronization effect of the neural network. However, changing the charge size and memristor feedback gain does not change the synchronization effect of the network. These findings provide new perspectives and methods for understanding and designing neural computing systems.

articleTitle: A Review of Fault Diagnosis Methods of Hidden Markov Model in Integrated Transmission Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The fault mechanism of the integrated transmission device is complex, and it is difficult to judge the fault only from the operating data. It is the key to improving the operation reliability of the equipment to obtain the degradation characteristic information of the development history of the trend fault accurately and establish an effective fault prediction model. The Hidden Markov Model (HMM) has the properties of a double random process describing the hidden state and observed state, which is similar to the degradation process of equipment to some extent, so it has become the research focus of the fault prediction model. In this paper, some hidden Markov fault prediction methods are summarized.

articleTitle: Multimodal Learning for Supporting Evidence Base Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Practicing evidence-based medicine relies on using a combination of various devices and technologies to support clinical decision-support. This multimodal approch improve prediction by fusing disparate data to better meet the precise diagnosis of diseases, such as medical images and histological information which can reflect the condition of the patient more comprehensively. Multimodal learning, however, utilizes techniques to process and find relationships between different types of data modalities to comprehend the case description as some clinical cues exist only in certain modalities. Actually in clinical practice, clinicians use imaging modalities like computed tomography (CT) scans or X-ray images beside non-image modalities like electroencephalogram (EEG) data or tabular data used in the electronic healthcare records to describe clinical cases. In this article we are presenting a multimodal machine framework that can be used for evidence-based practice using fine tuned MedCLIP transformer model to fetch relevant PubMed articles based on three different scenarios of usage where clinicians can provide multimodal queries in their search for relevant PubMed articles.

articleTitle: A Genetic Algorithm Based Feeder-User Connection Mapping Method with Limited Meter Data in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The dynamic topology of urban distribution power systems poses a significant challenge in accurately mapping energy supply districts, critical for illustrating feeder-household connections and ensuring efficient energy matching. Traditional approaches rely heavily on comprehensive smart meter data or the installation of new monitoring equipment, both of which are costly. This research proposes a novel genetic algorithm-based mapping technique that requires only energy consumption data. This approach leverages historical consumption patterns to produce feeder-user connection maps with high precision. A case study confirms the effectiveness of the algorithm in feeder-user connection mapping, and shows its potential for utility management optimization.

articleTitle: Electric Railway Vehicle Pocket Sliding Entrance System Fault Classification Using AI Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Railway vehicle entrances require accurate fault diagnosis and classification for fast, safe, and efficient maintenance. To this end, an entrance with the same specifications as a railway vehicle was constructed as a test bed to operate the door and collect both normal and abnormal data. The collected data was processed for feature extraction using statistical methods. Machine learning was then applied after removing highly redundant data through PCC to optimize the training data. As a result, the XGB model demonstrated the highest classification accuracy at 98.68%.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of TO Chopper Based on Fuzzy Fault Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The T0 chopper, as a crucial neutron optical device in time-of-flight neutron spectrometers, significantly influences the normal operation of the neutron spectrometer. Due to its prolonged operation in a special environment characterized by high radiation and low vacuum, it becomes challenging to accurately acquire the failure probabilities of its components. In this scenario, we introduce a reliability analysis approach for the T0 chopper utilizing a fuzzy fault tree, which integrates expert assessments with fuzzy set theory. Firstly, a fault tree for the T0 chopper is constructed, and qualitative analysis is conducted to identify the minimal cut sets. Secondly, we employ a blend of fuzzy set theory and expert linguistic assessments to quantify the occurrence probabilities of basic events, enabling the calculation of the fuzzy failure rate for the top event of the T0 chopper system. Subsequently, importance ranking was performed on the basic events, and the feasibility of this method was validated by combining it with historical operational data. Finally, considering the analysis results, specific risk mitigation measures are proposed for vulnerable aspects, laying the foundation for enhancing the reliability of the T0 chopper system.

articleTitle: A Developed Design of Power Generating Tiles
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Harvesting mechanical motion and converting it to electrical energy has increasing demands for enhancing the use of new sources of energy that are characterized by sustainable and environmental aspects. Design development is important for the best structure that delivers the required function and also for the Health Management of the Structure (SHM). Applying piezoelectric technology, e.g. the embedded cells in the sidewalk, shows a sustainable and clean source of electrical energy without using fossil fuel. In the current article, a developed stair-tile design is presented for power generation. The piezoelectric and mechanical techniques are applied to study power generation. Different input displacement cases are studied to simulate the free response and investigate how this will affect the generated energy. The results show that increasing the input displacement by changing the spring stiffness will have a higher response amplitude, which is better for piezo energy generation but might not be convenient for the users. The mechanical technique doesn't require high input displacement to increase the generated energy. The design is durable and applicable and both techniques can be used to generate sustainable and clean energy by tapping with continuous foot activity.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Rolling Bearing Based on MSCNN-CAM
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In the fault diagnosis of rolling bearings, traditional deep learning models such as convolutional neural network (CNN) may be difficult to extract multi-scale information from complex vibration signals effectively by using single-scale convolution kernel. Aiming at this problem, a fault diagnosis method based on multi-scale attention mechanism is proposed. Multi-scale convolutional neural network (MSCNN) is introduced in this method, and information is extracted from different scales by using convolutional kernels of different sizes to prevent the loss of important features in the extraction process. In addition, a channel attention mechanism module (CAM) is introduced to selectively filter out irrelevant features after multi-scale information extraction. The effectiveness of this method is tested on the bearing data sets of CWRU and QPZZ-II. The experiment of adding noise to data sets shows that the model has high fault classification accuracy, robustness and strong anti-noise ability.

articleTitle: Bearing Anomaly Detection Using Dynamic Loss-Guided Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Anomaly detection is an indispensable fundamental component of predictive maintenance. In recent years, an increasing number of autoencoder-based anomaly detection methods have been proposed to enhance the reliability of bearing operations. However, most encoders may introduce randomness and feature drift during the feature extraction process, leading to suboptimal detection performance and reduced robustness. This paper addresses this issue by proposing a bearing anomaly detection method called Dynamic Loss-Guided Autoencoder (DLGAE). The dynamic loss function reconstructs or constructs clustering centers by controlling the conflict degree between samples to overcome the balance issue between clustering and reconstruction in anomaly detection. Results tested on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that DLGAE exhibits excellent performance in bearing anomaly detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Fault Diagnosis Model Based on ISSA-VMD and CNN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Parameter constraints and local optimization of variational mode decomposition (VMD) can affect the fault diagnosis performance of rolling bearings. To solve this problem, a novel fault diagnosis model is proposed based on improved sparrow search algorithm (ISSA)-VMD and convolutional neural networks (CNN)-bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM) for rolling bearings. Firstly, the composite entropy indicator (CEI) is served as the fitness function for determining the optimal number of decomposed modes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> and the penalty factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex>. Secondly, employing VMD with these optimal parameters, the original bearing vibration signal is decomposed into multiple intrinsic mode functions (IMFs). Subsequently, nine crucial time-domain features are extracted to form a feature vector set. This set is then input into the CNN-BiLSTM model, facilitating automatic fault identification in rolling bearings. The approach establishes a robust methodology for effective signal decomposition and fault feature extraction.

articleTitle: Status Assessment Method of Armored Vehicle Engine Oil and Fluid System Based on ARO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The engine is an important component of armored vehicles, and effective detection of the engine status is an important guarantee for the vehicle and the personnel on board. The lubricating oil information can effectively respond to the health status of the armored vehicle engine, so it is very important to assess the status of the armored vehicle engine. This paper proposes an engine state assessment model based on Artificial Rabbit Optimization Algorithm optimizing Support Vector Machine. The model is simulated and the results show that the algorithm model can effectively assess the engine state and provide a reliable basis for engine maintenance.

articleTitle: Incipient Cracks Characterization Based on Jensen-Shannon Divergence and Wasserstein Distance
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Monitoring the structural health of Aerospace engine blades, which operate under complex and high-stress conditions, is vital for ensuring the safety and reliability of aircraft. Incipient cracks significantly impact the structural safety of aviation engine blades, and the precise characterization of incipient cracks is a tedious task. Eddy Current Testing (ECT), as a non-destructive evaluation technique, plays an essential role in this context, with recent technological advancements enhancing its capability to detect flaws. This study introduces a novel ECT signal processing method employing Jensen-Shannon divergence and Wasserstein distance for incipient cracks characterization. The efficiency of our method has been validated by comparing it with existing approaches, confirming its ability to precisely identify incipient cracks as minute as 0.02 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, even in cases with the same surface area but varying in length or depth. Our findings contribute to the precise characterization of incipient cracks, which is essential for maintaining engineering structures' safety and reliability under stress.

articleTitle: Bearing Fault Severity Assessment Method Based on Spectrum Energy Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: As the core component of rotating machinery, rolling bearings usually serve in harsh operating conditions, making it prone to performance degradation or even failure. Condition monitoring of bearings can prevent unexpected failures, minimize downtime, and reduce maintenance costs. Therefore, both academia and industry have shown significant interest in bearing condition monitoring. Confronted with the predictive maintenance in modern industry, various methods and techniques for bearing health assessment have been investigated. However, due to the complex operating conditions and environment of the equipment, the above methods are difficult to achieve satisfactory results in engineering practice. Therefore, a new bearing fault severity assessment method based on spectrum energy variation is proposed to overcome the above limitations. In this work, the frequency band energy is first extracted. Then, a dynamic anomaly indicator is introduced to detect spectrum narrowband energy abnormal associated with bearing degeneration. Finally, a bearing health index is established and divided into four stages to assess the bearing fault severity. Moreover, the performance of the proposed method is verified by bearing run-to-failure data. The result indicated that the proposed method is superior for bearing fault severity assessment in the engineering practice.

articleTitle: An Improved One-step Onsite FTU Health Condition Assessment Method Using Semi-supervised Graph Discrepancy Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The data-driven health condition assessment (HCA) methods of Francis turbine units (FTUs) have become an important part of hydropower unit prognostics and health management (PHM). Among them, some multi-step interdependent supervised models are designed to perform the assessment task. However, in the industrial scenarios, the status labels of data are rare and difficult to obtain, and the multi-step interdependent models will greatly increase the unreliability and inefficiency of the method. To make full use of rare status labels, it is necessary to model and excavate the spatial-temporal relationships hidden in the data. In this paper, an improved one-step onsite FTU health condition assessment method using semi-supervised graph representation discrepancy learning is proposed. First, through KNN algorithm, a small amount of labeled data are used to light up a large number of unlabeled data to construct graphs. This self-supervised method converts the health state data and the degradation state data into the graphs respectively, which improves the sample's state representation ability. Then, by using NT -Xent Loss to maximize graph discrepancy, the graph convolutional networks are trained as a graph representator, which reads the degradation graph and output the quantitative assessed degradation values. Therefrom, an end-to-end assessment model based on graph representation discrepancy learning is proposed to output quantified PDI directly from the input monitoring data. Comparative experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a competitive result.

articleTitle: Enhanced Incipient Cracks Classification in High Noise Environments Using PCA-SVM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Structural health monitoring is crucial for aircraft operation and maintenance, especially when it comes to engine blades. Engine blades are exposed to harsh external conditions for extended periods, making them vulnerable to various forms of damage and cracks, which pose significant safety concerns. Eddy current testing is a widely used technique in aircraft inspection and maintenance to identify cracks caused by factors such as fatigue and corrosion. In this study, a method for classifying incipient cracks is proposed, which significantly improves classification performance by extracting eight characteristic parameters, including mean, variance, maximum value, skewness, kurtosis, Kullback-Leibler divergence, Jensen-Shannon divergence, and Wasserstein distance. Crack classification is further improved by combining principal component analysis with support vector machine. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively classify cracks with different lengths and depths. By incorporating Principal Component Analysis, we have substantially improved the accuracy of the Support Vector Machine classification, especially in scenarios with high levels of noise. Notably, the enhancement in classification accuracy exceeds 20% when dealing with a noise level as high as 0 dB. Moreover, the implementation of our innovative approach, which combines PCA with distribution-based characteristic parameters, shows great potential for enhancing the safety and maintenance protocols for aircraft engines.

articleTitle: Fitness Assessment of AI-Based Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: AI-based systems differ strongly from other systems - and it is yet uncertain how this affects governing them, i.e., to which extent and how known system health management methodologies and processes need to be upgraded and partially re-invented to be fully suitable for AI-based systems. Our analysis indicates that the differences between AI-based cyber-physical systems and traditional systems impact health prognostics and management mainly due to the AI-based systems' foundation in information flows, their novel system architectures that become necessary to enable system-internal awareness to ensure that decision-making is based on accurate information, and their unique abilities, as systems that learn and thus change their behavior invalidate known health and performance indicators, often in unpredictable ways, and lifecycle management actions like updates, upgrades, or maintenance might no longer fit systems that adapted to their operational context. Based on this understanding, we propose to complement Health and Lifecycle Management methodologies for AI -based systems with a probabilistic model-based analysis of the system's information flows, giving insight into the expected timeliness and quality of information for various conditions, and thus whether the system is fit for its purpose. We see that estimating this fitness-for-purpose shows promise for various system health purposes, especially those ensuring trust in safety-critical AI applications.

articleTitle: Oxygen Excess Ratio Regulation for PEMFC Air Supply Systems Using Unscented Kalman Filter and Full-State Feedback Control
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Control-oriented research related to the air supply system of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) is of great importance for ensuring the safety and reliable operation of fuel cell-based energy systems. Key control objectives include regulating the oxygen excess ratio (OER), optimizing the net output power, and limiting the pressure difference between the anode and cathode. Particularly, regulating the OER plays an important role in supporting other health-conscious control objectives for PEMFC systems. Therefore, this paper introduces a fundamental OER regulation structure that combines the unscented Kalman filter with full-state feedback control. The proposed control structure achieves OER regulation with a reasonable time response and zero static error. This research provides a foundation for future comparative studies on different advanced control algorithms addressing various control objectives.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of AUV Propulsion System Based on Multi-Scale Dilated Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: The present study proposes a method for diagnosing thruster faults in autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) using the Multi-Scale Dilated Attention Convolutional Neural Network (MDACNN). The objective is to address the challenges posed by high computational complexity and limited generalization performance encountered by various fault detection methods employed in AUVs, which can be primarily attributed to the strong coupling and nonlinearity of their system modules. Firstly, in order to better capture the subtle features of thruster faults and fully extract the temporal features of vibration signals at different scales, the dilated convolution module is introduced into the multi-scale network. This approach can effectively identify thruster faults without increasing the number of parameters. Secondly, the efficient channel attention mechanism and MDACNN are combined to assign different weights to the feature information extracted at different scales, in order to enhance the network's emphasis on key features and improve the accuracy of fault diagnosis. Finally, features are further extracted through convolution, and a Softmax classifier is used for fault category classification. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify and diagnose thruster faults, and take timely measures for repair, ensuring the safe navigation of AUVs.

articleTitle: Can graph neural networks outperform in supervised classification of noisy acoustic signals? An industrial case study of hydroelectric generator
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: In this paper, we challenge the Graph Neural Network (GNN) to deal with the supervised classification task in case of noisy acoustic signals. The main goal is to verify whether employing GNN is particularly advantageous given the high complexity of its structure. The case study is the acoustic signals measured on the hydroelectric generator in a power plant. This type of industrial acoustic signal makes the classification task more challenging due to its noisy components such as the high background noise, etc. These factors could accidentally hide the characteristic features we are interested in classifying. A specific relative comparison with a traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approach was also performed to evaluate the performance of GNN.

articleTitle: TCAS: A Two-Channel Text Classification Model Based on Adversarial Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Text categorization has always been a research hotspot in the field of natural language processing. Although text classification models based on deep learning have achieved good results, the method of removing noise in the text preprocessing stage is usually relatively simple, which can affect the accuracy of classification when there is noise in the sample. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a two-channel text classification model that fuses adversarial samples. First, the samples to be classified are input into the adversarial network to generate adversarial samples, and the generated adversarial samples are feature extracted using DeBERTa and MLP. Meanwhile, feature extraction is performed on the original samples using RoBERTa and Bi-LSTM. Finally, a weighted fusion operation is performed on the features of these two channels to obtain the classification output. After experimental validation, the two-channel text classification model classification based on fused adversarial samples achieves 90.38% and 95.66% accuracy on MR and SST-Binary datasets, which is 4.15% and 4.12% higher than the baseline model, respectively.

articleTitle: Interpretable Graph Hyperinsulinemia Detection Model with Orthogonal Array Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Early detection of hyperinsulinemia in adolescents offers a promising opportunity to significantly reduce or even eliminate the risk of developing type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and other chronic non-infectious conditions. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), though complex, can provide precise forecasts, which helps narrow the gap between expected and actual diagnostic classifications in medical tasks such as detecting hyperinsulinemia, thus minimizing associated health risks. However, defining optimal hyperparameter configurations for GNNs remains a challenge. In this paper, we compare state-of-the-art models, including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Prior Structural Information-Graph Neural Network (PSI-GNN), and GraphSage (Graph Sample and AggreGatE). Our goal is to identify the best model for creating a balance between computational efficiency and prediction accuracy within a dataset collected nationally by the Healthcare Center in Serbia. We optimize performance through experiments with various hyperparameter settings and apply SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for a more precise determination of feature relevance, as evidenced by the reduced norm of activation vectors when compared with other centrality measures. Our findings reveal that the Taguchi orthogonal array optimization method, when applied to PSI-GNN, is the most computationally efficient. It yields superior performance metrics: an accuracy of 93.5%, an AUC of 97.4%, a precision of 92.2%, a recall of 96.5%, and an F1 score of 96.3%, with a running time of 273.2 seconds for 8 runs.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Fault Diagnosis for Reactants Starvation with Severity Levels in PEMFC Under Dynamic Load Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: This paper proposes an online fault diagnosis system for proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) to identify oxygen and hydrogen starvation faults at varying severity levels (low, medium, and high). The primary objective is to enhance the durability and reliability of PEMFCs for trans-portation applications, thereby contributing to the reduction of global CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions. Experimental data generated from a real PEMFC test bench are utilized to develop non-intrusive machine learning algorithms. The dataset comprises thousands of data points in both nominal and faulty conditions extracted from three cycles of the Worldwide Harmonized Light vehicles Test Cycle (WLTC). To reduce the dimensionality of the feature space, recursive feature elimination (RFE) is employed to select the most relevant features, including stack voltage, membrane resistance, stack power, pressure drop at the anode, flow rates at the cathode, and flow rate at the anode. These features are utilized to train classification algorithms, including variants of the support vector classifier (SVC), k-nearest neighbors (kNN), decision tree classifier (DTC), random forest classifier (RFC), and gradient boosting classifier (GBC). The results demonstrate that the support vector classifier with a radial basis function kernel (SV C-RBF) outperforms other classifiers, achieving an impressive accuracy of 98.76% and an F1-score of 98.80%.

articleTitle: The Physics-Based Mud Motor PHM Solution for Enhancing Drilling Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Improving mud motor reliability is vital in the drilling industry for enhancing drilling efficiency, minimizing environmental impact, and maximizing economic profit. Despite their long history of use, mud motors remain essential in drilling operations, converting hydraulic energy into mechanical force necessary for efficient well drilling. However, their frequent failures result in costly maintenance and operational disruptions, with traditional monitoring methods falling short and leading to suboptimal maintenance practices and unexpected expensive field failures. To address these challenges, we present a pioneering prognostics and health management (PHM) solution designed specifically for mud motors. This innovative approach predicts potential fatigue failures of the mud motor power section by estimating the remaining useful life (RUL), enabling operators to perform timely maintenance and optimize drilling processes. Our developed power section PHM model employs downhole measurements together with a numerical model of the considered power section to predict the RUL of the elastomer, a critical and highly sensitive component within the power section. Our approach, implemented within the PHM model, combines a high-fidelity physics-based model with data-driven techniques, ensuring accuracy and reliability in real-time applications or for post-job maintenance. Field trials conducted in various global locations demonstrate the effectiveness of our solution, which can be seamlessly integrated into drilling platforms to streamline maintenance systems and enhance well construction planning and execution. Our PHM solution represents a significant advancement in mud motor management practices, minimizing uncertainties surrounding RUL to support informed decisions on maintenance reruns, prevent over-maintenance, and reduce costs while improving operational efficiency. This solution signifies a paradigm shift in the oil and gas industry, offering actionable insights to mitigate risks, minimize nonproductive time, and strengthen operational reliability. By delivering precise prognoses of the power section elastomer liner's health, our PHM solution holds the potential to drive substantial cost savings and operational enhancements, marking a pivotal advancement in drilling technology.

articleTitle: RUL Estimation for Power Electronic Devices Using RNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) are commonly used in data-driven approaches to estimate the Remaining Useful Lifetime (RUL) of power electronic devices. RNNs are preferred because their intrinsic feedback mechanisms are better suited to model time-series data. However, the impact of RNN complexity on estimation accuracy is rarely discussed in the literature. This issue is important because choosing a lower-complexity model that delivers the same or similar performance as a higher-complexity model can increase implementation efficiency. In the paper, we use three RNN models, namely, the vanilla version, LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) and GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) to conduct RUL estimation for power electronic devices. We use two accelerated aging datasets, one dataset targeting the package failure of MOSFETs, and the other dataset targeting package failure of power diodes. Our study shows that a lower-complexity RNN does not necessarily deliver a lower performance. Similarly, a higher-complexity model does not assure a higher performance. As such, our work highlights the importance of selecting a proper neural network for RUL estimation not biased towards complex models. This is especially useful and important for implementing such RUL estimation techniques in embedded resource-constrained and speed-limited computins platforms.

articleTitle: A Continuous Learning Method for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Dynamic Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Rolling bearings are prone to faults due to their complex and harsh working environment, and accurate detection of their fault categories is crucial for maintenance prediction. The current deep learning based fault classification of rolling bearings has achieved significant results. However, when updating the model solely with unknown fault data, the performance of the model on the old classes significantly deteriorates, leading to catastrophic forgetting. To address this issue, this paper combines replay-based and constraint-based methods in continuous learning, proposing a novel approach called dynamic multi-teacher knowledge distillation for continuous learning (MKDCL). Firstly, MKDCL utilizes dynamic multi-teacher knowledge distillation for the first time to constrain the model in continuous learning. The student model learns from the teacher model with the highest accuracy in each fault category, avoiding the detrimental impact of poorly performing individual teacher models on the student model. During the training process, the cross entropy loss and dynamic multi-teacher distillation loss proposed in this article are combined, and the weight between the two losses is adjusted through a grid search algorithm, allowing the model to learn new knowledge while retaining old knowledge, enhancing the robustness of the model and improving accuracy. Secondly, MKDCL uses kurtosis as the criterion for selecting samples for storage, choosing samples closest to the average kurtosis of each fault category for storage. When new data arrives, the model is trained with both the new data and the data stored in memory, improving the model's accuracy. Finally, we use the Paderborn University (PD) dataset show that MKDCL achieves higher accuracy than classical continuous learning methods. Variance comparison validates the method's higher robustness.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Aero-Engine Based on Multi-Scale Channel Enhanced BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 Prognostics and System Health Management Conference (PHM)
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is one of the most important research directions for aero-engine predictive health management (PHM). It is critical to improve the safety and reliability of aviation engines. The key to achieving accurate RUL prediction lies in how to extract more important information from high-dimensional data-driven sequences through appropriate methods and effectively learn the information. Therefore, we proposes a multi-scale channel enhanced bidirectional LSTM (SE-MSC-BiLSTM) to achieve accurate RUL prediction of aeroengines. First, multi-scale convolution (MSC) is designed to extract features of different sizes from sensor monitoring signals. MSC is used for multiple convolutional kernels of different sizes, so that the model has a richer receptive field and can pay attention to the feature information at different time scales in the data. Secondly, channel attention is used to learn the correlation between multi-sensor data and achieve attention weight distribution.
